items.followUp: What is a malicious link? Give two warning signs that an e-mail containing one may be phishing.

rubric.why: Phishing is a deceptive attempt to obtain sensitive information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that phishing tricks people into revealing or giving away sensitive information.

rubric.why: Phishing e-mails commonly pretend to come from a trusted person or organization.
rubric.description: Gives one characteristic: pretending to be from a trusted source.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying impersonation or a misleading trusted appearance.

rubric.why: Phishing messages often pressure recipients to act quickly.
rubric.description: Gives one characteristic: creating urgency or threatening consequences.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying pressure to act quickly or a threat.

rubric.why: Phishing e-mails may seek sensitive details or direct users to harmful links or attachments.
rubric.description: Gives one characteristic: requesting sensitive information or including a suspicious link or attachment.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any one of these features.

modelAnswer: A phishing attack is an attempt to trick a person into revealing sensitive information by using a deceptive e-mail or message.
A phishing e-mail may pretend to come from a trusted person or organization.
It may create urgency or threaten consequences to make the recipient act quickly.
It may ask for passwords or other personal information, or contain a suspicious link or attachment.
